findings.statement: SERPINB5 is made almost only by epithelial cells (transit-amplifying and cycling cells in Smillie 2019), with a dominant-lineage share of the transcripts of [gene=SERPINB5; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.953]; the epithelial lineage is also dominant in all three other atlases (Garrido-Trigo 2023, Gubatan 2026, GSE282122), so the attribution replicates. The bulk rise is intrinsic: after adjustment for cell proportions the log2FC stays significant at [gene=SERPINB5; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=2.109]; Visium deconvolution also names epithelium as the in-situ source.

CHRDL2 is stromal (mainly Inflammatory Fibroblasts), with a stromal transcript share of [gene=CHRDL2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.939], and the lineage replicates in all three other atlases. The bulk rise is only partly composition: the retained fraction after adjustment is [gene=CHRDL2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.276], still significant, but the adjustment may over-correct because fibroblast activation also raises lineage scores. In Visium the deconvolution places the in-situ signal in smooth muscle while the composition-corrected source is the inflammatory fibroblast, so the exact producing cell is not settled.

CPXM1 is a stromal (WNT2B+ fibroblast) gene whose bulk increase partly survives cell-composition adjustment, with an adjusted log2FC of [gene=CPXM1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.057]; its neutrophil share is small, so it is not a neutrophil-influx marker. Replication in the other atlases is two of three.

PCDH17 is a stromal-lineage (endothelial) transcript that replicates in the three other atlases, but almost all of its bulk rise is explained by cell proportions: the retained fraction after adjustment is only [gene=PCDH17; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.098] (verdict partly_composition, adjusted change barely significant). Treat it as a marker of vascular or stromal expansion rather than a change inside the tissue; this weakens it for testing first. The adjustment can over-correct, so this is not proof of pure influx.

LAIR2 is a T/NK transcript (Tregs, CD8+ LP, NKs) with lineage replication in all three other atlases; the bulk change is partly composition, with an adjusted log2FC of [gene=LAIR2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.4441] that remains significant. T-cell influx therefore explains much of it, and a target claim rests on a per-cell increase in Tregs and cytotoxic cells.

LILRA1 behaves as a marker of myeloid and neutrophil influx: neutrophils make a share of its inflamed-mucosa transcripts of [gene=LILRA1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.502] and its bulk change loses significance after adjustment (adjusted padj [gene=LILRA1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_padj=0.105], verdict composition). Because adjustment removes the influx these genes report, this is not a target in a resident cell.

CEACAM4 is mostly neutrophil RNA, with a neutrophil share in inflamed mucosa of [gene=CEACAM4; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.87], so a bulk rise mainly reports neutrophil arrival.

XKR9 is epithelial (Immature Goblet, Enterocytes) with the lineage agreeing in two of three other atlases (Gubatan 2026, GSE282122; Garrido-Trigo 2023 points to plasma cells). Its bulk change is intrinsic, with a retained fraction after adjustment of [gene=XKR9; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.798]. Xenium, Visium and CosMx do not cover the gene, so there is no in-situ confirmation.

SDR16C5 is made by epithelial cells (transit-amplifying, cycling and immature goblet cells), replicated in all three other atlases, and its bulk rise is intrinsic with a retained fraction of [gene=SDR16C5; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.66] after adjustment.

CFB is mainly epithelial: Visium deconvolution names epithelium as the in-situ and composition-corrected source and CosMx detects it above background in epithelium, and the bulk change is intrinsic (adjusted log2FC [gene=CFB; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.8989]).

CEBPB, the genetics-first candidate, is a broadly expressed transcription factor: neutrophils make a share of its transcripts of [gene=CEBPB; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.698], with macrophages and plasma cells the main Smillie clusters. The genetic-target record predicts an effect in colon dendritic cells, and the cell record shows that cell is not the dominant source. The bulk increase is mostly composition (partly_composition, retained fraction low), so a CEBPB inhibitor would act on many myeloid cell types at once.

TUFM, the genetics-first candidate, is a ubiquitous mitochondrial gene (plasma cells and epithelial transit-amplifying cells in Smillie 2019) that does not rise in inflamed bulk tissue: its change is slightly down, with an unadjusted log2FC of [gene=TUFM; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; unadjusted_log2fc=-0.188], opposite to the genetic direction of inhibiting a gene that risk alleles raise. The genetic-target record predicts an effect in blood neutrophils, whereas the single-cell record shows epithelial and plasma cells as the main source. Single-cell and tissue data do not support it as an inflamed-mucosa target.

CHI3L1 is a fibroblast transcript in Smillie 2019, but neutrophils also make a large share in Gubatan 2026 (replication in two of three other atlases only); the bulk rise partly survives adjustment, with an adjusted log2FC of [gene=CHI3L1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3967], so it is both a tissue change and a marker of inflammatory cell arrival.

REG1B is epithelial (TA, goblet) and replicates in all three other atlases; its bulk rise is intrinsic, with an adjusted log2FC of [gene=REG1B; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.4585].

INHBA is stromal and myeloid (fibroblasts and macrophages) in Smillie 2019 and the lineage does not replicate in the other atlases; the bulk change is partly composition, with an adjusted log2FC of [gene=INHBA; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.6949], so the cell of origin is uncertain.

caveats: Composition adjustment can over-correct: lineage scores also rise when resident cells activate, so a partly_composition or composition verdict is not proof of pure influx.
Shares of transcripts compare cell types, not tissue abundance; dissociation protocols enrich some fractions.
Smillie 2019 has no neutrophils and GSE282122 has none either, so neutrophil attribution rests only on Gubatan 2026 and cannot be replicated.
The pool dossier flags a red safety light for CFB, which weighs against testing it first (dossier statement, not an atlas record).
REG1B rises in regenerating crypts according to the pool dossier, so inhibition could impair repair (dossier statement, not an atlas record).

Not examined in this run for lack of calls: CYP4X1 (composition intrinsic, epithelial), LYPD5, SGIP1, FIBIN, FJX1, OLFML2B, KLK10, MMP10, CXCL1, CXCL3, PDPN, SELP, GUCY1A1, LY96, RORC, CFAP90 and FIGNL1 beyond the neutrophil-share screen; the neutrophil screen flags CXCL1, CHI3L1, LY96, CEACAM4 and LILRA1 as neutrophil-heavy.
Spatial data (Xenium, Visium, CosMx) were checked for only SERPINB5, CHRDL2, CFB and XKR9; XKR9 is not covered.
